get.summary:
Start OAuth flow - redirect to provider.
# Errors
get.description: Returns an error if the provider is invalid, authentication is required but not provided, or service errors occur.

Handles both real OAuth flow and test bypass mode. Always answers with a
redirect: the browser arrives here by top-level navigation from the
provider, so a JSON error body would strand the user on a raw error page.
Provider-reported errors (e.g. a cancelled consent) and every internal
failure go back to `/login` with a fixed error code; the cause is logged,
never put in the URL.

get.summary: Legacy magic-link entry point: redirect to the frontend confirmation page.
get.description:
Emails used to link here directly, and this GET verified the email on the
spot. Mail scanners that prefetch links used the token up before the user
clicked, so it no longer has side effects: it only forwards the token, in the
URL fragment, to `/verify-magic`, where the user confirms with a button
(`POST /api/v1/auth/verify-magic`). Kept so links in emails sent before the
change still work; new emails link to the frontend page directly.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The magic link token from the email

303.description: Redirects to the /verify-magic confirmation page with the token in the fragment

post.summary: Confirm a magic link (backup to the 6-digit code).
post.description:
Answers exactly like `verify-email`: a `signup_token` in the body when the
account has no password yet, otherwise a session (cookies) for auto-login.
Nothing here goes into a URL, so the signup token never reaches browser
history or access logs.

400.description: Invalid, expired or locked link, the account is already verified and has a password, or a malformed request

AuthResponse.description:
Response body for successful authentication and for token refresh.

The JWT access token and refresh token are delivered exclusively as
`HttpOnly` cookies (the native-client body-token path was removed), so only
the non-secret session metadata is returned in the body. Login and refresh
return the identical shape, so they share this one DTO rather than a
duplicate `RefreshResponse`.

csrf_token.description: CSRF token for state-changing requests (also set as a readable cookie).

expires_at.description: Unix timestamp when the access token expires.

ChangePasswordRequest.description: Request to change password (for users who already have a password).

ClientErrorEvent.description: A browser error, deduplicated within its page load (`count` repeats).

api_route.description: For `api` errors: the route template the call used.

count.description: How many times this error happened in the page load.

island.description:
For `boundary` errors: the island whose boundary caught it. Mapped to
the island allowlist on the server; anything unknown is `other`.

message.description: The error message, scrubbed in the browser and again on the server.

network_failed.description: For `api` errors: the request never reached the server.

source.description: The script the error came from, or `external` for another origin.

status.description: For `api` errors: the response status, when the server answered.

ClientErrorKind.description:
What kind of browser error a report describes (OT-006). Unlike the enums
above it is the field's real type: an unknown kind is rejected outright, so
it can't become a metric label.

allOf.description: A script error, unhandled rejection, boundary error or failed API call.

oneOf.description: A script error, unhandled rejection, boundary error or failed API call.

The page finished loading, by a full load or an in-site navigation: the
denominator of the error rate. Never sampled.

allOf.description:
One Web Vital: LCP, FCP or TTFB for a full load, INP or CLS for a page
visit. Sampled.

oneOf.description:
One Web Vital: LCP, FCP or TTFB for a full load, INP or CLS for a page
visit. Sampled.

allOf.description:
A full page load or an in-site navigation, with its timings (Decision
6a). Sampled.

oneOf.description:
A full page load or an in-site navigation, with its timings (Decision
6a). Sampled.

allOf.description:
When an island became interactive or ready, from the start of the
navigation that showed it (Decision 6b). Sampled.

oneOf.description:
When an island became interactive or ready, from the start of the
navigation that showed it (Decision 6b). Sampled.

ClientIslandEvent.description: One island timing mark on the batch's page (Decision 6b).

ms.description: From the start of that navigation, in ms.

name.description:
The island's `TelemetryBoundary` name. Mapped to the island allowlist
on the server; anything unknown is `other`.

nav_type.description: The kind of navigation that showed the island.

ClientNavigationEvent.description:
A navigation to the batch's page (Decision 6a). The field is `nav_type`
because the event's own tag is `type`.

Any combination the schema allows is accepted; the server labels it
consistently: a `hard` load is always `view_transition=none` with no phases,
an `aborted` navigation has no durations, and a navigation without the
timings it needs is counted but not timed.

total_ms.description:
From the start of the navigation (0 for a full load) to the page being
usable and any transition having finished.

transition_ms.description: The view transition's animation, when it ran.

ClientReportBatch.description: One batch of browser reports from one page load.

page.description:
`location.pathname` without a trailing slash. Mapped to a page template
on the server; anything unknown is recorded as `other`.

page_load_id.description: Random ID of the page load, regenerated on sign-in and sign-out.

release.description: Release of the site the browser is running (commit SHA, or `dev`).

attribution.description:

selector `web-vitals` gives. Logged only for poor ratings, never a

value.description: Milliseconds, or the unitless score for CLS.
